items.titleEn: Gold prices remain under pressure as Fed minutes show central bank committed to cooling inflation
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Gold prices have dropped to session lows as the Federal Reserve remains firmly committed to raising interest rates to bring inflation down to its 2% target, according to the latest minutes of the central bank’s monetary policy meeting. Although the Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged in October, the minutes showed that committee members see cooling persistent inflation as their top priority. “Most participants expected inflation to remain elevated in the near term but to decline over time toward 2 percent, reflecting the waning of tariff-related price effects, a reduction in energy prices’ contribution to inflation, and a moderation of the pressures associated with the AI buildout. The vast majority saw upside risks to this outlook, citing higher energy prices and continued supply constraints with regard to refined fuel products,” the minutes said.

items.titleEn: As silver underperforms gold, has its bubble popped?
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - The ongoing threat of higher interest rates through year-end and into 2027 continues to support U.S. dollar strength and hangs over the precious metals market like a dark cloud. Rising opportunity costs have pushed gold prices to their lowest level since mid-September, with prices falling below $3,800 an ounce. Spot gold last traded at $3,732.90 an ounce, down more than 3% on the day. However, it's the silver market that is attracting the most attention Wednesday, with prices falling sharply below $45 an ounce. Spot silver last traded at $44.90 an ounce, down 5% on the day.

items.titleEn: Gold price follows the dollar in the short-term, but real yields over the long haul – Heraeus
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) – Gold ’s recent price correction has restored the precious metal’s inverse correlation with real yields, which broke down completely during its 2022-2025 rally, according to precious metals analysts at Heraeus. In an analysis of gold and bond yields published this week, the analysts noted that since hitting a record high of $5,600 per ounce in late January, gold has declined 33.5% to around $3,730. “Over the same period, the dollar index (DXY) has risen from 96.3 to 103.2 and the US 10-year inflation-protected real yield has climbed from 1.89% to 2.83%,” they said. “Last week’s hotter-than-expected CPI reinforced both headwinds and expectations of further Fed tightening.” Over shorter-term horizons, the dollar is one of gold’s most consistent price drivers. “Since 1990, the correlation between daily percentage changes in the gold price and DXY has been -0.31, and -0.43 this year,” the analysts said. “Put simply, dollar-up days have tended to be gold-down days. A 1% rise in DXY this year has typically coincided with a little more than a 2% fall in gold.”
